6th December 1933.
Mrs. Hudson E. Bridge,
Route 2, Box 1004,
Clayton, MISSOURI,
U.S. A.
Dear Irs. Bridge,
Please pardon the type written letter,
my excuse is that I am very busy and have had to write so
much long hand recently that my right arm is giving me
some trouble.
Your first letter reached me soon after
Dwight had arrived in Shanghai.
I showed it to him and he
told me a day or two later that he had written to you. Your
second letter of September 24th was forwarded to me in
Manila, and I thought when I received it that I would pro-
bably see you in person before any letter which I wrote to
you would arrive.
Unfortunately however, my affairs
here have taken a turn which have made it necessary for me to
cancel my trip home, at least for the time being.
I left
Manila on the afternoon of November 13th, and that morning
had the pheasure of welcoming to Manila John and Marjorie
Holiday.
Marjorie told me that when she passed through
Shangnai, Irom Japan to Manila, that she had called up Dwight,
only to learn that he was then on a tender bounde lor a
boat which would take him to Bali; that is the latest news
I have of your "wandering boy".
I am sure you will be glad
to know that he did some very
excellent work in Shanghai,
notably a full length portrait of Mrs. Chang, on of Judge
Purdy, who presides over the American court of China, a por-
trait
o1 Edwin Cunningham, American Consul General at Shanghai,
and several other portraits.
In all, I believe about ten.
I was very sorry to see him leave here, because he could have
secured many other orders, but apparently Dwight wished to
carry out his original project to travel on around the world.
1 hope to get away for home before the end
o1 December,
and will be lookkig forward to seeing you and the
other St.Iouis Bridges on my return.

Very sincerely,
